discovery: Invention and realization of the optical lattice clock

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / precision measurement
motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock (2001-2005), trapping thousands of neutral atoms at a 'magic' wavelength where the light shift on the clock transition cancels, combining the high Q of optical transitions with massive parallel interrogation. Ye transformed the concept into the world's most accurate and stable timekeepers, reaching systematic uncertainties near 10^-18 and below, resolving the gravitational redshift across a millimetre-scale atomic sample, and exploiting many-body quantum coherence. Katori demonstrated relativistic geodesy with transportable lattice clocks, including at the Tokyo Skytree. These instruments now drive the redefinition of the SI second, set stringent limits on drifts of fundamental constants and ultralight dark matter, and test general relativity in the laboratory. This is precision measurement as a route to discovery: a new instrument opening new physics, worthy of the Nobel Prize.
